corrected_fields.summary: This ECB Working Paper examines the resilience of the euro-denominated repo market during episodes of financial stress using transaction-level data and network analysis from 2021 to mid-February 2025. The paper finds that the institutional repo network exhibits a core-periphery structure with connectivity intensifying during stress periods, while trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable at the sectoral level. Notably, the euro repo market as a whole displays lower spreads during periods of elevated financial stress, indicating the market functions as a shock absorber rather than a source of contagion. [Disclaimer: Views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect official ECB positions.]
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: Understanding how the euro repo market functions during stress is critical for financial stability policymakers. The repo market is the largest segment of euro money markets, accounting for 56% of daily transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts. This research provides empirical evidence that the euro repo market maintains resilience during stress episodes, with the network structure and pricing mechanisms helping to absorb shocks rather than amplify them. The findings have implications for designing repo market regulations and financial stability frameworks. [Note: Author's personal research, not official ECB position.]
